sourceFiles.view.json: Declarative identity, input, state/event output ports, optional interaction and slots, plus all three layout tiers with min/preferred/max sizes and placement.
sourceFiles.types.yaml: Wes type package under types. view.json.input must name a Record contract; wrap lists/scalars in named fields. Read view_authoring types for syntax, constructors, constraints and time rules.
sourceFiles.View.tsx: Default export: defineView(definition, renderer). Import the generated definition from ./contract.
sourceFiles.view.css: Optional author styles. Import from the renderer to include them in the artifact.
sourceFiles.contract.ts: Generated before TypeScript checking. Input, Outputs, State, Event and EventOutputs types come from Wes contracts.

execution: Compilation never evaluates source. Views receive inputs, committed state and emit; they never own commands or source streams.
numbers: Use numericText for exact display and drawingNumber for checked plotting conversion; unsafe drawing conversions return undefined.
contracts: Contract validator executable: wes-view-build on PATH, or WES_VIEW_CONTRACT_TOOL.
diagnostics: JSON ok:false, diagnostics:[{code,message,file?,line?,column?}]. Failed builds retain the previous artifact.
workflow: Read workspace_context and view_toolchain first. The tool inventory describes the Wes backend host, not necessarily the agent terminal. Export the optional kit explicitly, install its locked dependencies with Node/npm on the build host, and invoke node wes-view-package.mjs. No repository checkout or PATH guess is needed. Discovery does not perform these actions. Read public input with value_read typed:true.

Read view_authoring types. Choose an explicit named Record input and output/interaction contracts; wrap list/scalar data in a field with a pure adapter. Generate contract.ts using the compiler; do not invent or copy a builtin contract.

Read view_authoring layout. Declare intentional tier sizes and placement; use actual allocation width instead of pane count or fixed screen breakpoints. Test a composed dashboard and a standalone host.
Use the supplied theme roles for meaning and CSS variables for layout. Do not fix a palette or font.
Build with the independent compiler, then check the compiled artifact. Verify normal, empty, duplicate identity, invalid and exact-number cases.
Install a checked artifact with the existing :package load and :view create commands discovered through help. Respect owner/revision checks.

prerequisites.provisioning: view_toolchain reports backend-host availability and a repository-free explicit export/setup path. Node/npm and dependency installation remain explicit build-host prerequisites. Discovery does not provision, compile, install a View, grant access or execute providers.

layout.units: columns and rows use the mounted host mono advance and line height; they are not CSS pixel ratios.
layout.bounds: Each axis: integer 1 <= min <= preferred <= max; max 512 columns and 200 rows. Declare all tiers for new Views. An absent layout uses host defaults.

placement.semantics: fill uses the slot width up to max; preferred stays near preferred width, can shrink down to min, and leaves spare slot space for alignment. The dashboard may override width and alignment; it owns the slot and weighted layout, the View owns its inner frame.

layout.height: Finite content has natural height inside dashboard cards; max.rows bounds the card viewport. Standalone expanded/window use a preferred-row viewport with host resizing and max-row caps. Live dashboard cards reserve preferred-row height: publications must never change it.
layout.preview: Render a bounded short summary. The host shows its complete natural height; min/preferred/max rows are summary guidance, not a crop. Never render the full input just because preview can grow.
layout.allocation: context.allocation supplies actual iframe CSS-pixel width/height and measured columns/rows; preferred is not a guarantee. The iframe height follows natural content under the tier cap, not the parent dashboard slot height. Do not use allocation.height to set whole-view height: that creates a measurement feedback loop. Use width for responsive geometry and bounded plot heights for content.
layout.containment: Reflow chrome, wrap long text, and keep overflow inside the View below min. Do not create sideways page scroll or hide unreachable controls. Nested slots have one parent viewport; avoid another whole-view resize grip.
layout.authority: Resize, tier, theme and dashboard placement changes preserve identity/state and never execute or replay sources.
acceptance: bounded preview with all controls visible
dashboard weighted slots and row-to-column reflow
theme/resize preserve selected state and emit no commands

verification: A checked/installed artifact is not proof of a successful UI render. Use view_render_status for a named live instance on the connected originating UI; draw acknowledgement confirms delivery, not visual correctness. No connected UI means unverified.
